item.title: BepiColombo space probe enters Mercury's orbit after eight-year journey
item.description: The mission aims to study all aspects of Mercury in the hopes of providing scientists with a better understanding of the planet and of the evolution of our solar system.

item.title: COP31 climate talks fail after EU and others reject final deal proposal
item.description: A new COP31 draft agreement had been published early on Sunday amid a row over fossil fuels, which have been a flashpoint at the talks.

item.title: Emergency workers recover at least six body bags after Indonesian factory fire
item.description: Video footage posted on social media by Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency (Basarnas), showed emergency crews looking through the charred remains of the building.

item.title: 15 people missing after Russian drone strike on Kyiv region
item.description: Timur Tkachenko, the head of the Kyiv Regional Military Administration, said the bodies of two people had been recovered from the rubble and that at least four people had been injured.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 22nd, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 22nd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Mongolia's power struggle deepens as Parliament approves president's resignation
item.description: Mongolia is facing growing political and economic uncertainty after Parliament approved the resignation of president Khurelsukh Ukhnaa. Rising inflation and fuel shortages are adding to economic pressures, while rival factions within the ruling People's Party compete for political influence.

item.title: Ukraine: Up to seven feared trapped beneath rubble near Kyiv after Russian attack
item.description: A Russian strike partially destroyed an apartment building in Dymer, north of Kyiv, on Sunday. Nine people, including a child, were evacuated as rescuers searched the rubble for up to seven others feared trapped.

item.title: Euronews' Attila Kert tapped to lead Hungary's public broadcaster
item.description: Euronews Hungary head Attila Kert has been tapped to run Hungary's public broadcaster, which faces an overhaul after years of bias criticism under Viktor Orbán. He pledges to restore credibility, launch streaming and probe Russian influence.

item.title: Japan: Mascot mania takes over Saitama with 200 colourful characters
item.description: More than 200 colourful mascots gathered in Saitama, Japan, delighting tens of thousands of fans with dancing, parades and photo opportunities. Among the stars was Kumamon, the country's famous black bear mascot.

item.title: Tracking site says Iranian tanker reportedly sailing through Strait of Hormuz does not exist
item.description: The US military said Saturday marked 130 consecutive days of its naval blockade against Iran, which it says is preventing the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps from exporting "billions of dollars in crude oil."

item.title: Portugal: Workers brave downpours to demand a more affordable life
item.description: Thousands of people marched through Lisbon, Portugal, on Saturday 21 November 2026, braving heavy rain to demand higher wages, better pensions and measures to tackle the rising cost of living. The demonstration came just days before Portugal's parliamentary budget vote.

item.title: Reported FBI hack 'not good' but could have benefits, Trump says
item.description: The reported breach comes amid a wave of tech outages in the US, which have impacted travel, communications and banking, as well as an internal system used by the National Security Agency.

item.title: Hot freezers, lost GPS and fake bombs: Europe's month of cyberattacks
item.description: Only three of the incidents tallied by Europe's main tech industry group have been linked to a culprit, and that ambiguity may be the attackers' strongest weapon.

item.title: COP31 climate deal in doubt after European Union rejects draft
item.description: The latest draft again failed to mention fossil fuels, which have become a flashpoint at the talks.

item.title: Gadi Eisenkot invites Netanyahu's Likud party for 'marathon' coalition talks
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot has until early December to form a new government after both his and Netanyahu's blocs fell short of a majority in Israel's October legislative elections.

item.title: Madeira's ocean survey finds evidence protection works – and some worrying signs
item.description: A survey by more than 200 specialists found that Madeira's marine reserves are working – but some species are still in peril.

item.title: Is Europe ready to judge workers by skills, not just diplomas? Who leads skills-first hiring?
item.description: Employers across Europe increasingly value skills while formal qualifications are still significant. Euronews Business takes a close look at which countries are most ready for a skills-first approach with experts explaining the gaps.

item.title: Suffolk village votes to ‘leave UK’ in protest over asylum seeker plans
item.description: Residents of Barnham back symbolic independence vote after government proposes accommodating around 930 asylum seekers at a nearby former RAF base.

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 22nd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: A five-star stay in Qatar: Luxury hotels and resorts to book
item.description: From beachfront resorts to skyscraper hotels overlooking the Arabian Gulf, Qatar is home to a growing portfolio of luxury properties.

item.title: Ukraine: Dashcam captures massive explosion on Lviv street
item.description: A dashcam captured the moment a Russian projectile struck a building directly ahead of a car in Lviv, forcing the driver to reverse. The attack killed two people and injured at least 10 others.

item.title: Salvage operation under way after cargo ship runs aground off French coast
item.description: French authorities are racing to prevent a stranded cargo ship from capsizing after it ran aground off the south-western coast. The Maltese-flagged vessel, which is carrying more than 100 tonnes of fuel, poses a potential pollution threat as salvage teams prepare to refloat it.

item.title: Iran attacks US bases in Bahrain as its tankers get ready to break the US blockade
item.description: The “no war, no peace” US-Iran confrontation appears to be moving towards a possible breaking point as Iran increases its military actions in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, while its critical attempt to break the US military naval blockade in the Persian Gulf appears to be imminent.

item.title: Video shows Mexican forces capturing 'El Chapo Isidro', FBI most-wanted cartel boss
item.description: Mexican special forces captured drug kingpin Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “Chapo Isidro”, during a raid in Sinaloa, with footage showing soldiers escorting him into an army vehicle.

item.title: Thousands take to streets in Portugal, France and Spain over rising living costs
item.description: Thousands of people demonstrated in Portugal and France on Saturday, calling for higher wages, affordable housing and action to tackle the rising cost of living. In Lisbon, workers marched despite heavy rain, while trade unions, Yellow Vest activists and youth groups gathered in Paris.

item.title: Paolo Bulgari, Italian jewellery tycoon, dies aged 89
item.description: The grandson of Bulgari's founder helped transform the family jewellery business into one of the world's most prestigious luxury brands. He led the Roman maison as chairman from 1984 and remained passionate about jewellery design throughout his life.

item.title: New documentary: Princess Kate speaks candidly about how cancer changed her body and mind
item.description: The Princess of Wales opens up about the physical and emotional impact of her cancer diagnosis in a deeply personal BBC documentary. Kate also reflects on her recovery, finding hope amid uncertainty and learning to live with a new perspective on life.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 21st, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 21st, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Real Madrid outpace Bayern Munich in revenue race as both clubs post record figures
item.description: Real Madrid have widened the financial gap over Bayern Munich, generating more than €1.2 billion in revenue in the 2025-26 season. The German champions are also approaching the billion-euro mark, while celebrating a record 500,000 members.

item.title: Estonia-Russia border closure sends residents rushing to cross before deadline
item.description: Families and travellers are queuing to cross from Russia into Estonia before all five road border crossings are shut on 1 December. The decision follows an alleged Russian-backed sabotage attempt, but has also raised concerns among people with relatives on both sides of the border.

item.title: Former Costa Concordia cruise ship captain released from prison on probation after nine years
item.description: The case dates back to January 2012, when the Costa Concordia ship struck rocks off the coast of Isola del Giglio in the Tyrrhenian Sea. The disaster claimed 32 lives.

item.title: Raccoon roast as a sustainable alternative to Germany's Christmas goose?
item.description: A chef from Thuringia serves the furry pest with red cabbage and dumplings, praising its tender meat. Could it become the new Christmas favourite?

item.title: Brazil ex-president Bolsonaro in intensive care over intestinal problem
item.description: The former Brazilian president was taken to hospital with abdominal pain, accompanied by military police.

item.title: Mexico captures FBI’s most-wanted cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’, triggering violence
item.description: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, one of the FBI’s ten most-wanted fugitives, was arrested in a military operation involving US intelligence cooperation. Gunfire, burning vehicles and panic among civilians followed the raid in northern Mexico. 11 people were killed.

item.title: Russian cargo ship still on fire after being struck by drones in Gulf of Finland
item.description: The United States announced sanctions against the Sparta II in early May 2022, just over two months after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Ukraine has also sanctioned the vessel.

item.title: Ballistic missile attack on Zelenskyy's hometown kills two people
item.description: The strike mainly targeted civilian infrastructure, Zelenskyy wrote on X. The attack comes after Russia vowed a 'painful' response to Ukraine's strike on the Crimean bridge.

item.title: EU budget: Costa pitches more cuts, Big Tech tax to break deadlock
item.description: European Council President António Costa proposes cutting the EU's 2028-2034 budget by nearly €200bn, a 10% reduction, to win over frugal countries. Cohesion funding is cut for the first time. A 3% digital services levy replaces a controversial corporate tax, and debt repayment is slowed down.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz: Athlete swims through war zone to expose war's environmental toll
item.description: British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh completed a 15-kilometre swim through the Strait of Hormuz over three days in November 2026, braving explosions and burning tankers nearby. His three-day challenge aimed to expose the environmental damage caused by the war with Iran.

item.title: European Union and Indonesia sign free trade deal after decade of talks
item.description: Trade between the EU and Indonesia was valued at €28.9 billion in 2025, with EU exports worth €10.2 billion and EU imports worth €18.7 billion.

item.title: Hagia Sophia's hidden tunnels uncovered as 420 metres of underground network cleaned
item.description: During cleaning and excavation works carried out at the site, significant remains were uncovered and carefully documented by archaeologists.

item.title: French President Macron warns of 'new level' of Russian aggression
item.description: The warning came after a series of airspace violations, reported sabotage attempts and an alleged assassination plot made headlines.

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 21st, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Japan: Autonomous air taxi completes passenger flight without a pilot
item.description: A pilotless electric flying taxi has carried a passenger during a demonstration, on Friday 20 November 2026, in Japan's Yamanashi Prefecture. The Chinese-built aircraft took off vertically and flew autonomously, offering a glimpse of a possible future for urban transport.

item.title: Anthropic worker claims to have solved famed 167-year-old maths problem with help of AI
item.description: Brian Greene, a professor of physics and mathematics at Columbia University in New York, called Alpöge's proof potentially "one of the greatest mathematical breakthroughs in the past two centuries."

item.title: Off the Record: Europe shrugs as Trump's Yalta knockoff flops
item.description: In this week’s newsletter, Euronews Political Correspondent Jorge Liboreiro unpacks the fallout from the much-hyped “Yalta 2.0”, describing the outcome as a political nothingburger.

item.title: Pentagon declassifies new UFO footage filmed by US military
item.description: The US Department of War has published its eighth release of declassified historical files on unidentified anomalous phenomena, with further documents expected to be made public.

item.title: Fossil fuel row sees COP31 talks spill into overtime
item.description: A number of countries, including France and Panama, released a letter on Friday insisting that a deal include "a clear transition away from fossil fuels."

item.title: Second judge blocks construction of Trump's massive 'triumphal arch'
item.description: Trump, who has embarked on a campaign to remodel Washington since his return to the White House in January 2025, has said the structure would be turned into a "top grade military complex."

item.title: Chronic loneliness linked to higher dementia risks in new study
item.description: A French research team tracked people’s loneliness and dementia risk over 30 years.

item.title: Putin a 'killer,' Zelenskyy says after Trump calls Russian leader his 'friend'
item.description: It comes after Russian forces launched a major wave of strikes against Ukraine from Thursday night into Friday morning, killing at least seven people in Kyiv and damaging key bridges across the Dnipro River.
